signals.title: [docs] Convert the seven card-grid library front doors from RST to MyST
signals.text: ## Why are these changes needed? MyST Markdown is the standard for Ray doc pages, and a lint check already rejects newly-added `.rst`. This is the second batch of the conversion of the existing hand-written prose under `doc/source/`, following #65467. The batch is the seven library front-door pages. They share one pattern: a `grid` of `grid-item-card`s, some `tab-set`s, `literalinclude` pulls, and a `toctree`. 1,889 lines, and 18% of all `.rst` page views over the last 90 days. | File | Lines | Constructs | | --- | --- | --- | | `tune/index.rst` | 299 | 3 tabs, 6 cards, 3 literalinclude, `callout`/`annotations` | | `ray-core/walkthrough.rst` | 132 | 3 cards, 4 literalinclude | | `data/data.rst` | 187 | 5 cards, 1 testcode | | `train/train.rst` | 233 | 10 cards, nested `div`, `raw:: html :file:` | | `ray-overview/installation.rst` | 548 | 2 tab-sets, 3 tables, 20 named link targets | | `ray-overview/ray-libraries.rst` | 378 | 17 cards | | `cluster/getting-started.rst` | 112 | 4 cards | The conversion is format-only. Every label name, `toctree` entry, directive, and prose line is preserved, so the rendered HTML should be unchanged. No URLs change: Sphinx maps `foo.rst` and `foo.md` to the same `foo.html`. Unlike #65467, this batch needs no CI or `BUILD.bazel` changes. None of the seven files is named in `doc/BUILD.bazel`, in a `.buildkite` rules fixture, or in `ci/ray_ci/doc`. `data/data.rst`'s one real `testcode`/`testoutput` pair stays covered by the `data` doctest rule's `source/**/*.md` glob. ## Card grids convert to native MyST Every card grid already in a `.md` page (`cluster/vms/index.md`, `cluster/kubernetes/index.md`, `ray-overview/index.md`, `serve/index.md`) is wrapped in `{eval-rst}` and left as RST. This batch uses native MyST fences instead: ```markdown ::::{grid} 1 2 2 2 :gutter: 1 :::{grid-item-card} **Title** ^^^ Body text. +++ ```{button-ref} some-label :color: primary Button text ``` ::: :::: ``` sphinx-design supports MyST first-class — its own docs are MyST and it ships a `snippets/myst/` tree. The `^^^` and `+++` separators are matched by `REGEX_HEADER`/`REGEX_FOOTER` and split out of the raw content lines before anything parses them, so they're format-agnostic. `GridDirective` and `GridItemCardDirective` are ordinary docutils directives registered through `app.add_directive`, which MyST dispatches exactly the way it already dispatches `{tab-set}` in a dozen `.md` pages today. The one thing to know: these directives call `self.state.nested_parse`, so under MyST their content parses as **Markdown**. Any RST left inside a native card renders as literal text instead of erroring. That's why the nested `button-ref`/`button-link`/`image`/`figure` directives all convert too, and it's the specific thing the render diff below was run to confirm. A follow-up PR converts the four existing `{eval-rst}`-wrapped grids so the tree ends up with one pattern rather than two. ## Conversions worth a second look - **`installation.rst`'s nightly-wheel table becomes a `{list-table}`.** It's a `====`-delimited RST simple table whose cells are named-target references. Keeping it as RST inside `{eval-rst}` was the first attempt and it silently broke all eight Linux wheel links, which resolved as internal anchors instead of the S3 URLs; see the verification comment. Inlining the URLs into the simple table isn't possible either, because cell text longer than the column ruler breaks it. So it becomes a `{list-table}` with `:widths: auto`, matching the MacOS and Windows tabs that were already list-tables. The page render-diffs identical. - **`tune/index.rst` had two link forms that don't survive transcription.** `` `Ray Serve`_ `` pointed at `../serve/index.html`, a relative `.html` URL that renders in RST but is a cross-reference target under MyST; it becomes `` {doc}`Ray Serve </serve/index>` ``. Separately, `` `terminating bad runs early <tune-scheduler-hyperband>`_ `` is an RST *external* link to a bare label name, so today it renders as `<a href="tune-scheduler-hyperband">` — a dead relative URL. Sibling lines in the same paragraph use `:ref:` for the same targets, so it becomes `{ref}`. **That is a deliberate rendering change and the one place the diff below is not empty.** Happy to keep the dead link if you'd rather this PR stay strictly format-only. - **`tune/index.rst` is the only file in the tree using the `callout` and `annotations` directives** (`doc/source/_ext/callouts.py`). Both `nested_parse`, so their content is now Markdown; the `<1>`/`<2>` annotation markers are literal text under both parsers. - **`train/train.rst`'s logo block** nests `div` inside `div` around a `raw:: html` with a `:file:` option. It converts to nested colon fences with a `{raw}` fence inside. - **`ray-overview/getting-started.md` linked to `../tune/index.rst`**, which would dangle after the rename. It becomes a `{doc}` reference. ## Verification - Static checks pass on all seven files: frontmatter parses, backtick and colon fences balance at every width, all 14 labels preserved, no residual RST outside fences, no `.rst`/`.html#` link forms, `testcode`/`testoutput` counts match the originals. - Read the Docs preview green under `fail_on_warning: true`, and `buildkite/microcheck` green. - `render_diff.py` against `/en/master`: 4 of 7 pages identical, 3 differing intentionally. **Full results, including three regressions the diff caught that the green build did not, are in [this comment](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/65470#issuecomment-5291959984).** ## Not a duplicate `gh pr list --repo ray-project/ray --state open` shows no other PR touching these seven files or this conversion, other than #65468, which changes six lines inside `installation.rst`'s extras table. Whichever lands first, the other rebases. ## Related issue number Part of the ongoing RST-to-MyST conversion of `doc/source/`, following #65467. Subsequent batches follow the same traffic-weighted ordering. AI assistance was used to prepare this change. ## Checks - [x] I've signed off every commit (`git commit -s`). - [x] I've run `scripts/format.sh` to lint the changes in this PR. - [x] I've included any doc changes needed for the change. - [x] Testing strategy - [x] Unit tests: not applicable; no `BUILD.bazel` or CI wiring changes in this batch. - [x] Release tests: not applicable. - [x] This PR is not tested (please justify below): the decisive checks for a conversion are the RtD preview build under `fail_on_warning: true` and the rendered diff against `/en/master`, both listed above.

signals.title: [doc] rst-to-myst: add the sphinx-design card-grid mapping
signals.text: ## Why are these changes needed? Stacked on #65469. Converting the seven card-grid front doors in #65470 exercised a part of the `rst-to-myst` skill that had no mapping at all: `grid`, `grid-item-card`, `grid-item`, `button-ref`, `button-link`, and `div`. The skill covered sphinx-design tabs and dropdowns but stopped short of cards, which are the dominant construct in batches 4 through 8. It also had no entry for RST named hyperlink targets (`` `text`_ `` plus a `.. _`text`: url` definition). `ray-overview/installation.rst` alone has twenty. ## What changed **Mapping rows** for the six sphinx-design directives above. **A construct note on card grids**, covering the two things that aren't obvious: - The `^^^` header and `+++` footer separators need no translation. sphinx-design matches them with `REGEX_HEADER`/`REGEX_FOOTER` in `cards.py` and splits them out of the raw content lines before anything parses them, so they're format-agnostic. - `GridDirective`, `GridItemCardDirective`, `div`, and Ray's own `callout`/`annotations` all call `self.state.nested_parse`, which under MyST parses their content as **Markdown**. RST left inside a native card doesn't warn — it renders as literal text through a green `fail_on_warning` build. Everything nested has to convert in the same pass, and the render diff is the only check that catches it. That second point also fixes a dangling reference: Verification step 4 already said the render diff is "the only step that catches Hard rule 5 or the `nested_parse` degradation below," and there was no such note below. Now there is. The note also records that four already-Markdown pages (`cluster/vms/index.md`, `cluster/kubernetes/index.md`, `ray-overview/index.md`, `serve/index.md`) wrap their grids in `{eval-rst}`, and says not to copy that into new conversions. A follow-up PR converts those four. **A construct note on named hyperlink targets** — inline them as Markdown links, except where an `{eval-rst}` table's cells reference them, in which case the definitions stay RST inside that same block so no target name is defined twice. **Two verified facts**, both checked against the pinned source rather than assumed: - `sphinx_design==0.7.0` supports MyST first-class. Its own docs are MyST, it ships a `snippets/myst/` tree, and its directives register through `app.add_directive`, so MyST's `{name}` dispatch reaches them like any other directive. - `_replace_numbers()` in `doc/source/_ext/callouts.py` discards its own result (`content.replace(...)` with no assignment), so the `<1>`-to-① substitution only happens in `CalloutIncludePostTransform`, over literal blocks. Annotation text keeps literal `<1>` markers under either parser. Flagging rather than fixing, since it's outside this PR's scope and the rendering is longstanding. ## Not a duplicate `gh pr list --repo ray-project/ray --state open --search "rst-to-myst"` returns #65469, which this is stacked on and which touches different sections of the same file. No other open PR touches `doc/.claude/skills/`. ## Related issue number Follow-up to #65469. Motivated by #65470, which deliberately doesn't carry this change, since a rule change buried in a content PR ships unreviewed. AI assistance was used to prepare this change. ## Checks - [x] I've signed off every commit (`git commit -s`). - [x] I've run `scripts/format.sh` to lint the changes in this PR. - [x] I've included any doc changes needed for the change. - [x] Testing strategy - The claims about `^^^`/`+++` splitting, `nested_parse`, and directive registration were read off `sphinx_design==0.7.0`'s own source (`cards.py`, `grids.py`, `extension.py`), not inferred. The native-grid pattern the note prescribes is the one #65470 ships and render-diffs. - Release tests: not applicable. - This PR touches `doc/.claude/` only, which no Bazel target or `.buildkite` rule references, so it pulls no CI suite.

Four pages are already Markdown but keep their sphinx-design card grids as RST inside an `{eval-rst}` block: | File | Cards | | --- | --- | | `cluster/kubernetes/index.md` | 6 | | `serve/index.md` | 5 | | `cluster/vms/index.md` | 4 | | `ray-overview/index.md` | 3 | That pattern predates native MyST card support and, until #65470, was the only card-grid precedent in the tree. signals.title: [Fix/n] Return External Consumer Bytes for Downstream Capacity to Activate Backpressure
signals.text: ## Description #64456 applies the block ref counter to track the object store memory and control backpressure signals based on downstream capacity, but this had lead to spilling in training pipelines. This is mainly due to backpressure not being applied to the terminal operator even though the external consumer is not consuming blocks quickly enough. This PR adds back the early return for `DownstreamCapacityBackpressurePolicy`'s `_get_downstream_capacity_size_bytes`, so that for terminal operators, the downstream capacity is the external consumer bytes tracked instead of 0. ## Related issues Fixes https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/64456.

signals.title: [Core] Fix prepared bundle leak and scheduling stall when removing an in-flight placement group
signals.text: ## Description Removing a placement group while bundle preparation is still in flight can leak prepared raylet resources and leave the GCS placement-group scheduling gate stuck. The scheduler already documents that a `PrepareBundleResources` callback may never fire (e.g. when the target node dies), but cancellation and removal still waited on that callback: - `MarkScheduleCancelled` only recorded the cancelled state; already-prepared bundles were not released because cleanup waited for `OnAllBundlePrepareRequestReturned`, which requires *all* prepare callbacks to return. - A prepare reply arriving after cancellation was folded into the tracker but still waited for the remaining callbacks before any cleanup ran. - `RemovePlacementGroup` never released `scheduling_in_progress_id_`, so a later pending placement group was never scheduled. This change makes cancellation- and removal-time cleanup independent of the prepare callbacks that may never arrive: - `MarkScheduleCancelled` now destroys the already-prepared bundles immediately (skipped only while committing, where the commit path already handles cleanup). - A prepare reply that returns after cancellation releases the just-prepared bundle immediately instead of waiting for the remaining callbacks. - `RemovePlacementGroup` releases the scheduling token it owns, and the creation callbacks only release the token when the callback's placement group still owns it, so a stale callback from a removed group cannot clear a newer group's token. ## Related issues Fixes #64693 ## Additional information No API or wire-format changes. The regression tests model a prepare callback that never returns by withholding the reply on the mock raylet client, so they are deterministic. ## Tests - `bazel test //src/ray/gcs/tests:gcs_placement_group_scheduler_test --test_filter=GcsPlacementGroupSchedulerTest.PlacementGroupCancelledAfterPartialPrepareReleasesPreparedBundle --test_output=errors` — fails on master (no `RemovePlacementGroupBundles` RPC for the already-prepared bundle), passes with this change. - `bazel test //src/ray/gcs/tests:gcs_placement_group_scheduler_test --test_filter=GcsPlacementGroupSchedulerTest.PlacementGroupCancelledAfterLatePrepareSuccessReleasesNewBundle --test_output=errors` — fails on master, passes with this change. - `bazel test //src/ray/gcs/tests:gcs_placement_group_manager_test --test_filter=GcsPlacementGroupManagerTest.TestRemovingLeasingPlacementGroupUnblocksPending --test_output=errors` — fails on master (the pending placement group is never scheduled), passes with this change. - `bazel test //src/ray/gcs/tests:gcs_placement_group_manager_test --test_filter=GcsPlacementGroupManagerTest.TestLateCallbackDoesNotReleaseNextPlacementGroupToken --test_output=errors` — covers the scheduling-token guard: a late creation callback from a removed placement group must not release the token a newer group now owns. Fails on master, passes with this change. - The surrounding placement-group cancellation tests in both files (`DestroyCancelledPlacementGroup`, `PlacementGroupCancelledDuringCommit`, `PlacementGroupCancelledDuringPreparedPut`, `TestRemovingLeasingPlacementGroup`) pass.

signals.title: [Autoscaler][V2] Add ALLOCATION_GATED status for scaleGate fast fallback
signals.text: ## Why are these changes needed? When an external controller (e.g. Kueue) blocks a worker group from scaling up by setting `spec.workerGroupSpecs[i].scaleStrategy.scaleGate` (for example, on a quota-exceeded group), the autoscaler previously had no way to distinguish this "gated" condition from a genuine allocation failure. A requested instance for a gated group would sit in `REQUESTED`/`ALLOCATED` until the allocate-status timeout elapsed before the scheduler could fall back to a lower-priority group. This PR introduces a dedicated `ALLOCATION_GATED` instance status so gated launches fail fast and the scheduler immediately falls back to another group, instead of waiting for the timeout. ### What changed - **Proto / state machine**: Add `ALLOCATION_GATED` to `Instance.InstanceStatus` in `instance_manager.proto`. It is a terminal status reachable from `REQUESTED`, mirroring `ALLOCATION_FAILED` (no cloud instance is ever allocated). - **`LaunchNodeError`**: Add a `gated` flag so the provider can signal a scaleGate block rather than a real failure. - **`KubeRayProvider`**: Detect gated worker groups on each sync (`_evaluate_scale_gates`), batch gated in-flight launches per request id, and emit gated `LaunchNodeError`s. Pending pods of gated groups are excluded from the fetched instances so they are not counted as launching/allocated. - **Reconciler**: Transition gated launches `REQUESTED -> ALLOCATION_GATED`, treat the status as inactive/terminal in cleanup, and surface it under `failed_instance_requests` in the autoscaling state. - **`CloudResourceMonitor`**: Deprioritize gated node types the same way as allocation timeouts (handler renamed to `allocation_timeout_or_gated`), so the scheduler picks a different group on the next cycle. ## Related issue number <!-- Link the tracking issue here, e.g. "Closes #XXXXX", or "N/A". --> N/A ### Tests - `python -m pytest python/ray/autoscaler/v2/tests/test_instance_util.py` (transition graph + reachable-from for `ALLOCATION_GATED`) - `python -m pytest python/ray/autoscaler/v2/tests/test_node_provider.py` (scaleGate detection, gated in-flight launch fast-fail, nil-gate cases) - `python -m pytest python/ray/autoscaler/v2/tests/test_priority_selection.py` (`ALLOCATION_GATED` marks node type unavailable) - `python -m pytest python/ray/autoscaler/v2/tests/test_reconciler.py` > Note: these require the proto to be regenerated so `Instance.ALLOCATION_GATED` > is available in `instance_manager_pb2` before running. ## Duplicate-work check Searched open PRs/issues for scaleGate / `ALLOCATION_GATED` / autoscaler v2 Kueue fallback and found no existing PR covering this change.

On `master`, the function is stored directly in `map_args` and serialized with every task submission. Large captured UDF state therefore consumes object-store memory approximately in proportion to the number of shuffle-map tasks. ### Benchmark Compared `master` against this branch using 500,000 rows and 4 local CPUs. signals.title: [LLM] Fix shell injection vulnerability and error handling in clear_d…
signals.text: ### Description Fixes a shell injection vulnerability and broken exception handling in `ray.llm`'s `clear_directory` utility. The previous implementation used `subprocess.run(f"rm -r {dir}", shell=True, check=False)` wrapped in a `try...except FileNotFoundError` block. This was flawed because: 1. `shell=True` with string interpolation introduces a potential command injection vector if the directory path is ever derived from dynamic inputs. 2. `subprocess.run` with `shell=True` executes `/bin/sh`. It will *never* raise a Python `FileNotFoundError`, making the exception block dead code. 3. Because `check=False` was passed, if `rm -r` failed due to actual permission errors or a read-only filesystem, it would silently fail without raising an error, causing a silent storage leak of LoRA weights. This PR replaces the shell invocation with the Python standard library's `shutil.rmtree(dir, ignore_errors=True)`, which is immune to shell injection, cross-platform, and correctly handles missing directories natively. **Why this is not duplicating an existing issue or PR:** Searched GitHub issues and open PRs for `lora_utils.py` and `clear_directory` shell injection; no existing work or reports were found. **Test commands run and their results:** - `pre-commit run --files python/ray/llm/_internal/common/utils/lora_utils.py` (Passed) - Verified locally via an isolated Python script directly importing and testing `clear_directory` on both existing and missing directories (Passed). Heavy `ray[llm]` tests were skipped due to network timeouts downloading `vLLM` / Triton binaries, but the core logic is fully validated. *Note: AI assistance was used to identify this vulnerability and draft the fix.*
signals.author: vikky781

signals.title: [serve] Declare __all__ in ray.serve.request_router
signals.text: ## Why `python/ray/serve/request_router.py` re-exports the public request-router extension surface, but declares it implicitly through `# noqa: F401` imports rather than explicitly through `__all__`. This declares it. The seven names are each decorated `@PublicAPI(stability="alpha")` at their definition site and documented in the Serve API reference at `doc/source/serve/api/index.md` under their `serve.request_router.*` path. `doc/source/serve/advanced-guides/custom-request-router.md` and its `doc_code/custom_request_router.py` teach users to import from this module. So the change records an existing contract rather than creating a new one. It also makes the surface visible to the API-doc consistency check. `API._is_public_reexport()`, added in #65340, treats a name in a public module's `__all__` as public regardless of where its implementation lives, but it requires an *explicit* `__all__` entry, which this module didn't have. ## Coordination This is a small mechanical change, so per `AGENTS.md` it's worth saying it was coordinated rather than volunteered. It follows from a ruling Richard Liaw gave on Ray's API location policy: a private definition re-exported through a public module's `__all__` is compliant, and the test that matters is whether users have to import a private package. Declaring the surface here is the fix that ruling implies. Happy to close this if the Serve team would rather handle the module differently. ## `ReplicaResult` is deliberately excluded It's the one name in the file left out of `__all__`, because unlike the other seven it carries no API annotation (`class ReplicaResult(ABC)`, no decorator) and has no reference-page entry. Including it would newly assert a public contract instead of recording one. Its import keeps an F401 suppression since the re-export is still in use. **This is the one judgment call in the PR and it's yours to make.** If Serve considers `ReplicaResult` part of the public extension surface, say so and I'll add it. `PowerOfTwoChoicesRequestRouter` is out of scope: it's absent from both this module's re-exports and the autosummary, so it needs a separate decision. ## Removing the per-import suppressions The seven declared names lose their `# noqa: F401` comments. A name listed in `__all__` counts as used, so pyflakes and ruff no longer flag it. `ReplicaResult` keeps its suppression. ## Testing Verified statically: - `ruff check python/ray/serve/request_router.py` — passes. - `black --check` and `ruff format --check` — already formatted. - Full `pre-commit run` on the changed file — all applicable hooks pass (ruff, black, pydoclint, docstyle, import order, semgrep). - Confirmed the declared `__all__` is exactly the set of seven names in the `serve.request_router.*` autosummary block, with no extras and nothing missing. **Not verified locally: `api_policy_check`.** It needs a Ray build, and master's Python source doesn't import against a released binary, so I'm relying on CI for that check rather than claiming a local run. The expected effect is on the resolve check only. I'm specifically *not* claiming this clears the `tracked_doc_debt` entries for these symbols: those fail the must-be-documented check, which #65340 explicitly left untouched. If CI shows any of them can drop, I'll follow up separately rather than bundling it here. ## Duplicate check No open PR touches `python/ray/serve/request_router.py`. #65410 (`[serve] Enforce type checking on the scheduling/routing modules`) touches `_private/request_router/request_router.py` but not this module, so no conflict. ## AI assistance AI-assisted, per `AGENTS.md`: the analysis and the patch were drafted with Claude Code, and I reviewed every changed line.

signals.title: [serve][llm] Add Native Anthropic Messages API (/v1/messages) Support
signals.text: ## Description Adds first-class Anthropic Messages API support to Ray Serve LLM for vLLM-based deployments. This allows Anthropic-compatible clients, including Claude Code, to communicate directly with Ray Serve LLM without an additional translation proxy such as LiteLLM or Claude Code Router. The initial implementation supports: - `POST /v1/messages` - `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` - Streaming and non-streaming message responses. - Standard ingress and direct-streaming deployments. - **Vanilla vLLM deployments.** SGlang fallbacks on import failure, P/D disaggregation and data parallel deployments are outside this PR's scope. ## Related issues - Closes #64965 ## Implementation - Added Ray wrappers and alpha public APIs for vLLM's Anthropic request, response, token-counting, and error models. - Extended `LLMEngine`, `LLMServerProtocol`, and `LLMServer` with `messages` and `count_tokens` operations. - Initialized and delegated requests to vLLM's `AnthropicServingMessages`. - Added `AnthropicIngress` (which inherits from `OpenaiIngress`), reusing the existing ingress model resolution, LoRA routing, handle caching, session affinity, and deployment configuration. - Translateed internal vLLM errors into Anthropic-compatible error payloads at the HTTP boundary. - Preserved vLLM-generated Anthropic SSE events for streaming responses. - Added `build_anthropic_app` with support for both standard ingress and direct streaming. - Extended the mock vLLM engine with Anthropic routes and responses. - Added tests covering model imports, route registration, builder behavior, error responses, token counting, and streaming/non-streaming requests. ## Testing ### pytest ``` PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -v \ python/ray/llm/tests/serve/cpu/configs/test_anthropic_api_models_backends.py \ python/ray/llm/tests/serve/cpu/deployments/routers/test_anthropic_ingress.py \ python/ray/llm/tests/serve/cpu/deployments/routers/test_anthropic_http.py \ python/ray/llm/tests/serve/cpu/deployments/routers/test_builder_ingress.py -k Anthropic ``` ### API I tested this using the `anthropic==0.106.0` & `vllm==0.26.0` python library, and **have not used Claude Code (yet).** Testing infra had the following specs: - signals.title: [Core] Add job level configuration to enable/disable lineage reconstruction
signals.text: ## Description Lineage reconstruction is currently provided by default as part of ray. The feature provides the capability to automatically track and re-execute any lost progress. However, this comes at the sacrifice of additional overhead per object created and task submissions that are transparent to user level code. The drawbacks can be undesirable if the application layer has other needs for fault tolerance that lineage reconstruction in core is unable to provide. This PR introduces a job granularity config that enables users to configure whether they want lineage reconstruction to be enabled for the task and actors created in that job while keeping the rest of the cluster's lineage reconstruction mechanism enabled. ## Related issues ## Additional information

signals.title: [serve] Deflake test_handle_deleted_on_crashed_replica
signals.text: After the Router is killed (ray.kill), the deployment can only scale to 0 once the Controller notices that the Router replica has died and drops the handle metrics it owns. The Router did not have health_check_period_s set, so detection took up to the 10s default, the same size as the bare 10s wait_for_condition the test gave the entire drain. In a reproduced failure the crash was detected 9s after the kill and the downscale decision came soon after 10s, but the test had already given up after 10s. The fix is to health check the Router every 1s, as another deployment in this test already does, and give the three post-kill waits the 20s that sibling test test_handle_deleted_on_non_serve_actor already uses for the same drain.

signals.title: [serve][doc] Document the '#' constraint on deployment names
signals.text: ## Why this change #65215 ("[serve] remove deprecated Serve APIs") turned a deployment name containing `#` from a `FutureWarning` into a hard `ValueError`: ```python # python/ray/serve/deployment.py # '#' is the replica ID delimiter, so it cannot appear in a name. if "#" in name: raise ValueError(...) ``` The constraint isn't documented anywhere. The `@serve.deployment` docstring says only that `name` uniquely identifies the deployment within the application, and no page under `doc/source/serve/` mentions a character restriction. So a reader who picks a name containing `#` now gets a runtime error with nothing to point them at. This adds the restriction and the reason to the `name` argument. `Deployment.options()` tells readers to "refer to the `@serve.deployment` decorator docs for available arguments," so the single edit covers both public surfaces. The reason given is accurate: `ReplicaID.to_full_id_str()` joins app name, deployment name, and unique ID with `#`, and `ReplicaID.from_full_id_str()` splits on it, so a `#` in a deployment name would corrupt round-tripping. ## Not a duplicate - `gh pr list --state open --search "deployment name validate"` and `"serve deployment name docstring"` return nothing covering this. - #65215, which introduced the hard error, is merged and did not document it. ## Testing Docstring only; no runtime code path is touched, so there's no behavior to test. The documented behavior is already asserted by the `pytest.raises(ValueError)` cases in `python/ray/serve/tests/unit/test_build_app.py` that #65215 added. `pre-commit run --files python/ray/serve/api.py` passes, including `pydoclint` and the Ray docstyle check. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to find the undocumented constraint and draft the wording. I reviewed every changed line and verified the delimiter claim against `python/ray/serve/_private/common.py` before submitting.

signals.title: [cherry-pick][2.58.0][Data] Check object store utilization instead of any spilling in release tests (#65222)
signals.text: Cherry-pick of #65222 (merge commit `68bbf43df11d8df2cb4a5ddfbebd4c2831a1d228`, authored by @bveeramani) onto `releases/2.58.0`. Clean pick, no conflicts — release-test tooling and config only (`release/ray_release/command_runner/_anyscale_job_wrapper.py`, `release/ray_release/command_runner/_prometheus_metrics.py`, `release/ray_release/tests/test_anyscale_job_wrapper.py`, `release/release_data_tests.yaml`, `release/release_multimodal_inference_benchmarks_tests.yaml`; +199/-53). No Ray runtime code is touched. ## Description Ray Data release tests currently fail if there is *any* object spilling. The backpressure policy only kicks in on cluster-wide object store utilization rather than per-node, so uneven object distribution produces tiny spills (e.g. ~6 GiB over a whole job) that fail otherwise-healthy tests — the autoscaling map-batches test has been flaky for this reason. This replaces the "no spilling at all" check with a check on peak object store utilization, failing only when a job exceeds 100% of object store capacity. Ray Data targets 50% utilization but can exceed it due to secondary copies, so 100% is the guarantee the current policy actually makes and is stable over time. The release test YAMLs are updated to use the new utilization threshold instead of the spilling flag. Picking this into `releases/2.58.0` so the 2.58.0 release test runs aren't blocked by spurious spill-based failures. ## Related issues Related to #65222 ## Additional information Not a duplicate: no existing cherry-pick PR for #65222 targets this branch (checked open and closed PRs). Checks run: - `git cherry-pick -x -s` applied cleanly; the resulting diff is byte-identical to the master change (verified with `diff` of both `git show` outputs). - `bazel test //release:test_anyscale_job_wrapper` — PASSED in 38.2s. - `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` — all applicable hooks passed. - AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this cherry-pick; reviewed by the submitter. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: [Serve] Add enable_strict_max_ongoing_requests deployment flag
signals.text: Mitigation for #46893: `DeploymentResponse._to_object_ref()` blocks until the replica finishes computing instead of resolving once the request is scheduled (a regression since Ray 2.10, because unary calls are routed through the streaming reject/accept handshake). Add an opt-in deployment option `enable_strict_max_ongoing_requests` (default True; behavior unchanged for existing deployments). When set to False on a unary deployment, the router computes `with_rejection=False`, so `send_request_python` falls through to the plain `handle_request` branch and `.remote()` returns a regular ObjectRef. `_to_object_ref()` then resolves at scheduling time, restoring the pre-2.10 chaining pattern `await asyncio.wait_for(response._to_object_ref(), timeout=N)`. Trade-off: in-flight rejection is skipped for that deployment, so the router's queue-length cache becomes the only guard against overshooting `max_ongoing_requests` (identical semantics to how Serve already handles Java replicas). This is a mitigation, not the core fix, and does not close #46893. - DeploymentConfig: new bool field (default True). - serve.proto: `optional bool` field so an unset value (older controller during a rolling upgrade) falls back to the Python default (True). - DeploymentSchema + decorator + schema<->deployment conversions. - Router: capture the flag from the deployment-config long poll and combine it with the existing capability gate when deciding rejection. - Tests: proto round-trip (incl. rolling-upgrade fallback), router config wiring, router opt-out routing, and an e2e regression test asserting `_to_object_ref()` resolves before the request completes.

signal.title: [serve][llm] Surface engine errors on the direct-streaming ASGI app
signal.text: ## Description vLLM's **engine error handler** reads `app.state.server` to flip `should_exit` and stop the uvicorn server its launcher created. `VLLMEngine.build_asgi_app` calls only `build_app` and `init_app_state`, neither of which sets it. So on the direct-streaming path, every `EngineGenerateError` / `EngineDeadError` raises `AttributeError` inside the handler, and that replaces the engine error, and therefore clients get 'State' object has no attribute 'server' instead of the real failure. ## Solution Supply a dummy object that just tolerates an attribute write `types.SimpleNamespace()`. Nothing reads `should_exit`; `terminate_if_errored` only assigns it. With the read satisfied, the handler runs on to `create_error_response(exc)` and returns vLLM's real error. Discarding the write is safe: `should_exit` only stops vLLM's uvicorn loop, which Ray never runs — Serve restarts replicas via `LLMServer.check_health`. ## Reproduction Stand up a server with the following script and environment variables `RAY_SERVE_LLM_ENABLE_DIRECT_STREAMING=1` and `RAY_SERVE_ENABLE_HA_PROXY=1`. ``` # serve_app.py from ray import serve from ray.serve.llm import LLMConfig, LLMServingArgs, build_openai_app llm_config = LLMConfig( model_loading_config=dict( model_id="qwen", model_source="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", ), deployment_config=dict( autoscaling_config=dict(min_replicas=1, max_replicas=1), ), ) serve.run(build_openai_app(LLMServingArgs(llm_configs=[llm_config])), blocking=True) ``` - Before ``` { "error": { "message": "'State' object has no attribute 'server'", "type": "InternalServerError", "param": null, "code": 500 } } ``` - After ``` { "error": { "message": "EngineCore encountered an issue. See stack trace (above) for the root cause.", "type": "InternalServerError", "param": null, "code": 500 } } ``` ## Related issues > Link related issues: "Fixes #1234", "Closes #1234", or "Related to #1234". ## Additional information ### Why is this bug only discovered when we upgrade to vLLM 0.27.0? `app.state.server` was always missing in Ray: only vLLM's launcher sets it, and Ray runs no uvicorn loop. In 0.26, handlers were registered per exception type: a bad request stayed a `ValueError` and matched a handler that never reads `state.server`. Only a genuine engine death reached the one that does, which release tests never provoked. In 0.27, `generate()` wraps bad requests as `EngineGenerateError`, routing routine 4xx traffic through that handler and exposing the `AttributeError`.

signal.title: [docs] Lowercase "Ray dashboard" across the docs
signal.text: ## Why this change "Dashboard" is a generic noun, so it stays lowercase next to a product name for the same reason "autoscaler" does. That's the convention #65239 settles, on @win5923's reasoning in [this review comment](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/65239#issuecomment-5283520022). This PR applies it across the docs. Splitting it out from the rule change keeps each one reviewable on its own: #65239 is the rule and the tooling, this is the mechanical sweep, and the diff here is casing with no prose rewrites. Same split as #65423, which retires "Ray Pod." **This depends on #65239 landing first.** If the convention changes in that review, this sweep changes with it. ## Scope All of `doc/source`, `.md` and `.rst`. 215 replacements across 53 pages, in prose: body text, headings, front matter and `.. meta::` descriptions, a glossary term, table cells, image alt text, and link and cross-reference text. Three commits, each reviewable on its own: the Kubernetes pages, the same term across the rest of the docs, and then the bare "Dashboard" that the first two left behind. The first commit covers `cluster/kubernetes/`, which is where #65239 scopes its Vale ruleset. The second extends the same convention to the rest, so it holds on every surface rather than only where the tooling happens to point: `ray-observability/`, `serve/`, `ray-core/`, `train/`, `ray-security/`, `ray-overview/`, the non-Kubernetes `cluster/` pages, `data/`, `rllib/`, and `ray-references/`. Headings are included deliberately. This guide requires sentence case for every heading, so "## Step 5: Access the Ray Dashboard" was already a defect on two counts. **The `ray-observability/getting-started` page title changes**, from "Ray Dashboard" to "Ray dashboard." That's the canonical dashboard page, so it's the most visible line in the diff and worth a deliberate look. Cross-references to it that don't set their own text pick the new title up automatically. ## Applied by script, reviewed by hand The sweep ran from a fence-aware script rather than find-and-replace, because a blind pass would have hit literal blocks and rewritten CLI output. It tracks Markdown code fences, treats MyST directive fences such as ```` ```{admonition} ```` as the prose they contain, and tracks rST literal blocks introduced by both `.. code-block::` and a trailing `::`. I reviewed all 162 replacements and each of the 9 exclusions individually. ## Deliberately not changed **Nine uses inside literal blocks**, because the rule governs prose. Eight are shell comments, five of them `# Step 7: Check Ray Dashboard...` in `k8s-ecosystem/ingress.md`. The ninth is literal CLI output in `user-guides/kubectl-plugin.md` (`Ray Dashboard: http://localhost:8265`), where changing it would misreport what the command prints. That leaves a page or two with a lowercase heading above a capitalized shell comment. I'd rather flag that than quietly edit code blocks in a prose sweep. Happy to include the eight comments if a reviewer prefers consistency within the page. **One use in `cluster/kubernetes/configs/static-ray-cluster.tls.yaml`**, a comment in a sample manifest rather than a docs page. **Nothing, as it turns out.** An earlier revision of this description claimed 217 bare capitalized "Dashboard" uses were being left alone. That number was wrong: the command behind it piped `grep -o` output into a `grep -v` filter that could never match, so it counted every occurrence of the word including the ones inside "Ray Dashboard". The real figure was 93, and the third commit sweeps the 54 of those that are the generic noun. What stays capitalized is listed above. **`README.rst` and the `python/` docstrings.** Eight files outside `doc/` use the term, mostly in docstrings that render into the API reference. Different surface, different owners. ## Bare "Dashboard" The third commit covers the 54 uses of a bare capitalized "Dashboard" that the term sweep left behind, which otherwise put "the Dashboard" next to "the Ray dashboard" on the same page. Most are a pure case change. Fifteen needed an article, because the prose used the word as a bare proper noun: "expose Dashboard outside the Cluster" becomes "expose the dashboard outside the Cluster", and three sentences opening "Dashboard is..." become "The dashboard is...". The installation extras table is the one place where a bare lowercase "dashboard" would have read badly, sitting in a list of Ray library names ("Core, Dashboard, Cluster Launcher"). Those rows and the tip below them now say "Ray dashboard". Left capitalized, because these aren't the generic noun: - CloudWatch's Agent, Dashboard, and Alarm config files, plus Grafana's Dashboard and Default Dashboard. - The literal **Open Dashboard** button label in the History Server UI. - Title and label positions where any word would capitalize: the "Dashboard (Web UI)" section title, a `Dashboard` tab label, and a `**Dashboard**` list label. - Twelve uses inside literal blocks, one of which is dashboard log output. ## Six adjacent lines Lowercasing one word of an otherwise title-case heading reads as a botched edit, so where that happened the whole heading goes sentence case: - `cluster/configure-manage-dashboard.md`: "Configuring and Managing Ray Dashboard" to "Configuring and managing Ray dashboard," plus the two link texts and one `:ref:` text that mirror that page title. - `ray-observability/user-guides/profiling.md`: "Ray Dashboard View" to "Ray dashboard view." - `ray-core/internals/token-authentication.rst`: "Ray Dashboard Flow" to "Ray dashboard flow." One more of the same kind in the first commit: alt text in `user-guides/kuberay-dashboard.md` read "KubeRay dashboard List of RayJobs" after the swap, so "List" lowercases too. ## Known cosmetic wart `user-guides/kuberay-history-server.md:13` now reads "see [Ray dashboard](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/ray-observability/getting-started.html)" against a target whose published title is still title case. This PR retitles that page, so the two converge once it lands. The sentence is redundant as written either way. ## Testing No code, no API, no behavior change. Most replacements are identical in length. The ones that aren't are the fifteen that gained an article and the installation table rows, so rST title underlines needed checking rather than assuming: one title, "Set up Dashboard" becoming "Set up the dashboard", grew past its underline and is fixed. Verified against `master` that the change introduces no other short underline anywhere in `doc/source`. Verified with Vale 3.12.0, running the ruleset from #65239 against this branch: the `Ray Dashboard` and `KubeRay Dashboard` swaps go from 44 alerts to **0** on the paths that ruleset scopes, and `doc/source/data/` holds at 170 with no new alerts. Vale doesn't cover the other paths in this PR, and it has no rule for the bare noun at all, so the rest was verified by hand against a categorized list of every occurrence. Verified by hand that nothing in the repo references any of the changed heading strings, so no cross-reference or link text goes stale. Nothing here is enforced in CI. The Vale pre-commit hook remains scoped to `doc/source/data/`. ## AI assistance Written with AI assistance (Claude). The script is mine, I've reviewed every replacement and exclusion individually, and I can defend the change end to end.

signal.title: [Autoscaler][V2] Add ALLOCATION_GATED status for scaleGate fast fallback
signal.text: ## Why are these changes needed? When an external controller (e.g. Kueue) blocks a worker group from scaling up by setting `spec.workerGroupSpecs[i].scaleStrategy.scaleGate` (for example, on a quota-exceeded group), the autoscaler previously had no way to distinguish this "gated" condition from a genuine allocation failure. A requested instance for a gated group would sit in `REQUESTED`/`ALLOCATED` until the allocate-status timeout elapsed before the scheduler could fall back to a lower-priority group. This PR introduces a dedicated `ALLOCATION_GATED` instance status so gated launches fail fast and the scheduler immediately falls back to another group, instead of waiting for the timeout. ### What changed - **Proto / state machine**: Add `ALLOCATION_GATED` to `Instance.InstanceStatus` in `instance_manager.proto`. It is a terminal status reachable from `REQUESTED`, mirroring `ALLOCATION_FAILED` (no cloud instance is ever allocated). - **`LaunchNodeError`**: Add a `gated` flag so the provider can signal a scaleGate block rather than a real failure. - **`KubeRayProvider`**: Detect gated worker groups on each sync (`_evaluate_scale_gates`), batch gated in-flight launches per request id, and emit gated `LaunchNodeError`s. Pending pods of gated groups are excluded from the fetched instances so they are not counted as launching/allocated. - **Reconciler**: Transition gated launches `REQUESTED -> ALLOCATION_GATED`, treat the status as inactive/terminal in cleanup, and surface it under `failed_instance_requests` in the autoscaling state. - **`CloudResourceMonitor`**: Deprioritize gated node types the same way as allocation timeouts (handler renamed to `allocation_timeout_or_gated`), so the scheduler picks a different group on the next cycle. ## Related issue number <!-- Link the tracking issue here, e.g. "Closes #XXXXX", or "N/A". --> N/A ### Tests - `python -m pytest python/ray/autoscaler/v2/tests/test_instance_util.py` (transition graph + reachable-from for `ALLOCATION_GATED`) - `python -m pytest python/ray/autoscaler/v2/tests/test_node_provider.py` (scaleGate detection, gated in-flight launch fast-fail, nil-gate cases) - `python -m pytest python/ray/autoscaler/v2/tests/test_priority_selection.py` (`ALLOCATION_GATED` marks node type unavailable) - `python -m pytest python/ray/autoscaler/v2/tests/test_reconciler.py` > Note: these require the proto to be regenerated so `Instance.ALLOCATION_GATED` > is available in `instance_manager_pb2` before running. ## Duplicate-work check Searched open PRs/issues for scaleGate / `ALLOCATION_GATED` / autoscaler v2 Kueue fallback and found no existing PR covering this change.

signal.title: [WIP]: Add writable cgroups guide
signal.text: ## Description Add a KubeRay user guide documenting how to enable Ray resource isolation (`--enable-resource-isolation`) on non-GKE containerd Kubernetes clusters using an NRI (Node Resource Interface) plugin. The plugin selectively grants writable cgroup access to annotated Ray pods without requiring privileged containers. The `nsdelegate` mount option on the node's root cgroup provides the kernel-enforced security boundary. The guide has two tracks: 1. Manual, step-by-step node setup, intended for cluster administrators 1. A non-production quick-start guide intended for AI developers wanting to use Ray with resource isolation on Kubernetes. Both tracks culminate in deploying a RayCluster with `enable-resource-isolation: "true"` and verifying that Ray creates its cgroup hierarchy inside unprivileged containers. ## Related issues <!-- Related to https://github.com/ray-project/ray/issues/ insert issue number if one exists --> ## Additional information - The NRI plugin source lives at https://github.com/pmengelbert/nri-writable-cgroups. - The annotation key (`writable-cgroups.nri.io/enable`) is configurable via the plugin's `--annotation-key` flag. - The existing GKE-specific writable-cgroups guide is unchanged; this guide targets clusters without GKE's built-in `writableCgroups` feature. - Validated on AKS. Expected outputs are included but have not been verified on EKS or other platforms. - `nsdelegate` remount does not persist across reboots; this is documented as a known limitation.

signal.title: [core] Add per-call RetryOnTimeoutPolicy to RetryableGrpcClient; opt in GetClusterId
signal.text: ## Why are these changes needed? A `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` on the cluster-ID fetch maps to `TimedOut`, which `IsGrpcRetryableStatus` deliberately never retries (that predicate feeds an unbounded retry queue). The fetch was a single all-or-nothing RPC with the whole connect budget as its deadline (30s on the Python standalone client path), so one deadline spent queueing on a GCS busy with a node registration storm was fatal to the connecting process — observed as fleet-wide bring-up deaths at 400 nodes on Ray 2.56. **Fix: generalize the existing retry infrastructure instead of adding a bespoke loop.** `RetryableGrpcClient::CallMethod` gains an opt-in per-call `RetryOnTimeoutPolicy`: - Each attempt gets a bounded per-attempt deadline, clamped to an **absolute overall deadline** derived from the call's `timeout_ms` — so retries can never exceed the caller's budget. - A timed-out attempt is re-sent after a **full-jitter exponential backoff** delay (uniform in `[0, min(100ms·2^attempt, 2s)]`). Jitter is the point: hundreds of clients that timed out on the same overloaded server at the same moment must not re-fire in lockstep. - Non-timeout errors keep the existing semantics (UNAVAILABLE/UNKNOWN → reconnect queue; everything else fails fast). Calls without the policy are unchanged. `GcsRpcClient::GetClusterId` is the only opt-in (hand-written instead of the `VOID_GCS_RPC_CLIENT_METHOD` macro to attach the policy), with per-attempt deadline `gcs_rpc_server_connect_timeout_s`. `GcsClient::FetchClusterId` shrinks back to a single sync call; it now `RAY_CHECK`s a non-positive budget instead of silently normalizing it (an invalid budget is an operator error and should fail loudly), and its final-failure `Disconnect()` behavior is unchanged. With the C++ default 5s budget this stays effectively a single attempt; the Python 30s budget becomes ~6 chances to land in a queue gap. An earlier revision implemented this as a hand-rolled attempt-counting loop inside `FetchClusterId` with a test-only virtual seam; this revision replaces that with the per-call policy in `RetryableGrpcClient` so there is one retry mechanism, it is reusable, and it adds jitter. Companion PR (server-side half of the same incident, independently mergeable/revertable): #64845. ## Related issue number None found — searched open PRs/issues for GetClusterId / connect retry before opening. Not a duplicate of in-flight work. ## Checks - [x] I've signed off every commit (DCO). - [x] I've run pre-commit on the changed files. - [x] Testing strategy — new `//src/ray/rpc/tests:retryable_grpc_client_test` exercises the policy against a real gRPC server with a freezable handler: `RetriesTimedOutAttemptsUntilSuccess` (attempts time out while frozen; a later attempt succeeds after unfreeze; ≥2 requests observed server-side) and `DeliversTimedOutWhenBudgetExhausted` (handler stays frozen; final status is TimedOut, delivered no earlier than the overall budget). Ran locally (macOS, `--dynamic_mode=off`): passes, along with `//src/ray/gcs_rpc_client/tests:gcs_client_test`, `gcs_client_reconnection_test`, `gcs_client_injectable_test`, `accessor_test`. (`global_state_accessor_test` fails on my machine because it hardcodes port 6379, which a local redis service occupies — pre-existing, unrelated.) Per the repo's AI contribution policy: AI assistance was used to develop this change; every changed line was reviewed and the tests above were run locally.

signal.title: [core] Isolate NodeInfoGcsService.GetClusterId on a dedicated lightweight-reads io_context
signal.text: ## Why are these changes needed? `GetClusterId` is a lock-free read of an immutable value (`gcs_node_manager.cc`), but its handler is posted to the single-threaded `node_manager_io_context` shared with `RegisterNode`, `GetAllNodeInfo`, `CheckAlive`, etc. During mass node registration the loop's queue delay exceeds client deadlines, and `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` maps to `TimedOut` which `IsGrpcRetryableStatus` deliberately never retries — so every connecting process's cluster-ID fetch dies on a constant-value read: ``` [gcs_client.cc] Failed to get cluster ID from GCS server: TimedOut: RPC error: Deadline Exceeded ``` We hit this as a full cluster bring-up collapse at 400 nodes (~60k potential worker processes) on Ray 2.56. `gcs_server_rpc_server_thread_num` cannot help (it only sizes completion-queue polling threads, which never run handlers). **Fix: isolate on an existing axis instead of adding dispatch machinery.** The GCS already isolates workloads with dedicated io_contexts (`GcsServerIOContextPolicy`). This PR adds a `lightweight_rpc_reads_io_context` entry there, plus a small `RPC_SERVICE_HANDLER_CUSTOM_AUTH_IN_IO_CONTEXT` macro variant that posts one handler to an explicit io_context (`_RPC_SERVICE_HANDLER` now delegates with the service's `main_service_`, so all other handlers are unchanged). `GetClusterId` is the only opt-in; `CheckAlive` — which is starved by the same storms and causes false node-death — can follow in a later PR. An earlier revision of this PR ran the handler inline on the gRPC polling thread. That worked, but it created a new hazard class: any future inline handler that gets slow stalls completion-queue polling for the whole server — exactly the failure mode of #55904, reverted in #59448. A dedicated io_context gets identical starvation immunity while a slow handler hurts only itself, and it reuses the GCS's existing isolation pattern (~10-line server diff instead of a new template axis through `ServerCallImpl`). The new io_context is lag-probed and health-check-critical (it sits on every client's `Connect()` path). Companion PR (client-side half, independently mergeable/revertable): #64847. ## Related issue number None found — searched open PRs/issues for GetClusterId / io_context starvation before opening (closest, orthogonal: #64422 GCS passive-mode refactor). Not a duplicate of in-flight work. ## Checks - [x] I've signed off every commit (DCO). - [x] I've run pre-commit on the changed files. - [x] Testing strategy: - New `//src/ray/rpc/tests:grpc_server_client_test` case `DedicatedIoContextHandlerRepliesWhileServiceIoContextNeverRuns`: the service's main io_context is never run; only a handler posted to the dedicated io_context can reply. - New `//src/ray/gcs/tests:gcs_server_rpc_test` case `GetClusterIdNotDelayedByNodeManagerIoContextBacklog`: blocks the node_manager io_context with a task that waits until released and asserts a 2s-deadline `SyncGetClusterId` still succeeds (fails with DEADLINE_EXCEEDED pre-fix). - Ran locally (macOS, `--dynamic_mode=off`): both targets pass. Per the repo's AI contribution policy: AI assistance was used to develop this change; every changed line was reviewed and the tests above were run locally.

signal.title: [Data] Support Arrow string-view and binary-view arrays in custom serialization
signal.text: ## Why are these changes needed? Ray's custom Arrow data serializer (`ray/_private/arrow_serialization.py`) has no handler for Arrow `string_view` / `binary_view` arrays (added in Arrow 16), so `_array_to_array_payload` raises `ValueError: Unhandled Arrow array type: string_view`. Consequences today: - **Under pytest** (`is_in_test()`): `ray.put()` / `ray.data.from_arrow_refs()` on any table containing a view column **crashes** with the error above. - **Outside tests**: every such table silently falls back to whole-table Arrow IPC serialization — slower and defeats the zero-copy-slice truncation this serializer exists for. Repro from the issue: ```python import pyarrow as pa, ray t = pa.table({"x": pa.array(["hello world, long string", "hi"], type=pa.string_view())}) ray.data.from_arrow_refs([ray.put(t)]) # crashes in pytest; IPC fallback otherwise ``` ## What does this PR do? Adds a dedicated payload handler for view arrays: - **validity bitmap**: sliced/bit-shifted like all other array types - **views buffer**: truncated to the slice using its fixed 16-byte-per-element width - **variadic data buffers**: passed through as-is — views store absolute offsets into these buffers, so they cannot be truncated without rewriting every view View types are detected with a `getattr` guard so pyarrow < 16 is unaffected. Verified locally (pyarrow 24.0.0): full-array, sliced (including non-byte-aligned offsets with nulls), and table-reduce round-trips all succeed through the custom path with no IPC fallback, and the views buffer is properly truncated on slices. ## Related issue number Fixes #59951 ## Checks - [x] I've signed off every commit (DCO) - [x] I've run pre-commit hooks (black + ruff) on changed files - [x] Unit tests added: `string_view_array` / `binary_view_array` cases in `python/ray/data/tests/test_arrow_serialization.py` (gated on pyarrow >= 16) - [ ] Release tests N/A

signal.title: [Data] Support appending a subset of columns to a Lance dataset.
signal.text: ## Description `Dataset.write_lance(..., mode="append")` fails when the data being appended contains only a subset of the target dataset's columns. On append, the sink sets the write schema to the full existing dataset schema, and the positional `RecordBatchReader.from_batches(schema, ...)` path then errors on the columns the incoming blocks don't provide (`reorder_columns_by_schema` → `Table.select` on a missing field), surfacing as a confusing `LanceError` / `OSError` instead of anything actionable. This PR makes **APPEND** align each block to the dataset schema and **null-fill the columns the block omits** — the missing columns become null for the newly appended rows, analogous to how Iceberg/Delta handle schema evolution on append. If a block contains a column that is *not* in the target dataset, a clear `ValueError` is raised (adding brand-new columns is out of scope; select the existing columns first via `ds.select_columns(...)`). Scope / compatibility: - Only `SaveMode.APPEND` changes. `CREATE` / `OVERWRITE` keep their existing strict behavior (still use `reorder_columns_by_schema`). - No public API change — composes with `ds.select_columns(...)`. - Extension types (e.g. `arrow.json`) and nested types are handled when building the null-filled columns. Before (fails): ```python import ray, lance, pyarrow as pa uri = "/tmp/lance_subset" lance.write_dataset( pa.table({"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": [4, 5, 6], "c": [7, 8, 9]}), uri, mode="overwrite" ) # Data provides only (a, b); the table is (a, b, c) ray.data.from_items([{"a": 10, "b": 40}]).write_lance(uri, mode="append") # -> OSError: LanceError(Arrow): ... KeyError: 'Field "c" does not exist in schema' After (this PR): the append succeeds and the new rows have c = null. Related issues N/A Additional information Tests added in python/ray/data/tests/datasource/test_lance.py: test_align_block_to_schema_reorders_fills_and_validates — unit test for the alignment helper: reorders columns, null-fills missing columns, and raises on columns not in the target schema. test_null_column_supports_extension_and_nested_types — null-column construction for extension (arrow.json-like) and nested types. test_lance_write_append_fills_missing_columns_with_null — end-to-end: appending (a, b) rows to an (a, b, c) table writes c as null.

signal.title: [Security] Private vulnerability reports are being acted on without any response to the reporter
signal.text: I am opening this issue because I am increasingly concerned about how private security reports are being handled in this repository. This is not a new vulnerability disclosure. The technical details, reproduction steps, and proof-of-concept material are already available to the maintainers in the private advisories referenced below. On July 4, 2026, I submitted two private vulnerability reports: - GHSA-3pfc-79r8-p8r7 — unsafe deserialization in `ray.data.read_numpy` - GHSA-797j-745w-c46h — unsafe deserialization in `ray.train.torch.TorchCheckpoint.get_model` Both reports have now been sitting in Triage for more than a month without any maintainer acknowledgement, triage response, remediation update, or coordination message to me as the reporter. That alone would already be disappointing for high-severity security reports. However, in this case the repository history shows that these reports are clearly not simply unseen. ## GHSA-3pfc-79r8-p8r7 The `ray.data.read_numpy` issue has already been fixed on `master`. PR #64684 was opened on July 11 and merged on July 15. It changes `read_numpy()` to default to `allow_pickle=False`, adds an explicit opt-in for pickle loading, and addresses the inability of callers to disable the previous hardcoded `allow_pickle=True` behavior. This is the core remediation described in my private report. More importantly, the regression test added by that PR explicitly references the private advisory ID `GHSA-3pfc-79r8-p8r7`. So the project has unquestionably received and acted on this report. Despite that, nobody has acknowledged the advisory, updated its status, or responded to me through the security-reporting channel. The currently released `ray==2.56.1` still contains the vulnerable hardcoded `allow_pickle=True` implementation, while the fix is present on `master` and the `releases/2.57.0` branch. I do not understand why a security report can be used to implement and test a fix, including adding a regression test that explicitly names the private GHSA, while the advisory itself is left completely unanswered. ## GHSA-797j-745w-c46h The same communication problem exists with the TorchCheckpoint report. Three days after I submitted it, PR #64586 was merged documenting that `TorchCheckpoint.get_model()` calls `torch.load(..., weights_only=False)` and that this can execute arbitrary Python code through pickle. That PR added a security warning, but it did not remove the unsafe deserialization behavior or provide the safe-mode opt-out described in my report. The current `master` branch and the `releases/2.57.0` branch still unconditionally call `torch.load(..., weights_only=False)` in `get_model()`. In other words, the underlying behavior reported in the advisory remains present. The remediation so far is documentation telling callers that the checkpoint source must be trusted. There may be a legitimate design discussion here. Ray may decide that loading full `nn.Module` checkpoints necessarily requires pickle-backed deserialization and therefore should remain a trusted-source operation. However, the report also specifically concerns the fact that `get_model()` unconditionally uses `weights_only=False`, including when a caller expects to load a state-dict checkpoint, with no public API allowing the caller to choose the safer loading mode. Whether the project considers the documentation warning to be complete remediation, intends to provide a safe loading path, considers part of the report accepted and part rejected, or has some other assessment is exactly the kind of triage decision that should be communicated through the private advisory. It has not been. I am intentionally not publishing the proof-of-concept code or additional technical exploitation details in this issue. What concerns me here is the handling of the reports themselves. Researchers should not have to infer the status of their private reports by watching unrelated public commits and pull requests. If a report is valid enough to produce a security fix, add regression tests referring to the private GHSA, or cause maintainers to publicly document the exact unsafe-deserialization primitive, then it is valid enough to receive a basic acknowledgement in the private security channel. At minimum, I would expect acknowledgement that each report was received, a clear triage decision, clarification of whether the current changes are considered complete remediation, affected and patched version information where applicable, and normal coordination with the reporter regarding advisory publication and CVE handling. Leaving high-severity reports unanswered while simultaneously acting on them in the public repository is not a reasonable vulnerability-handling process. Could someone responsible for Ray security please review both advisories and provide an actual status update? I would also appreciate clarification on who currently owns vulnerability triage for this repository, since the documented security-reporting mechanism does not appear to be producing any communication back to reporters.

signal.title: [Data] Fix ResourceBudget backpressure causing pipeline stall
signal.text: ## Why are these changes needed? Two interacting bugs in `ResourceBudgetBackpressurePolicy` can cause a Ray Data pipeline to stall indefinitely — CPU/GPU idle, Object Store filling up, no error logged, no progress. Reproducing this requires enough intermediate output to pressure the Object Store; small pipelines won't hit it. ### Background `ResourceBudgetBackpressurePolicy` blocks an operator from submitting new tasks when **either**: (a) the operator's `incremental_resource_usage` (CPU/GPU/memory) exceeds its budget, or (b) the operator's Object Store budget for task outputs is below `obj_store_mem_max_pending_output_per_task`. When either fires, the operator enters `backpressured:tasks(ResourceBudget)` and stops scheduling. ### The two bugs **Bug 1 — `OutputBackpressureGuard.should_unblock` doesn't distinguish Object Store–blocked from CPU/GPU-blocked.** The liveness relaxation in `should_unblock` relaxes an upstream operator's output backpressure when a downstream operator has no active tasks and can't submit — so upstream can finish and release CPU/GPU/memory. This helps when downstream is blocked on condition (a). But when downstream is blocked on condition (b) — its Object Store budget for task outputs is exhausted — relaxing upstream only writes *more* output into the already-full store while downstream still can't schedule. The relaxation feeds the stall it's meant to prevent. **Bug 2 — `update_budgets` unconditionally allocates shared resources to over-reserved operators.** Each scheduling iteration, `update_budgets` recomputes every eligible operator's budget as its unused reservation plus a share of the remaining shared resources. Even when an operator's Object Store usage already exceeds its reserved resources (unused reservation is zero), it still receives a share of the remaining shared resources — restoring a positive budget, letting it submit more tasks, and further draining the shared resources that other operators depend on. **How they compound:** Bug 2 keeps the upstream operator's budget alive so it keeps producing output. Bug 1 relaxes the upstream's output backpressure so that output flows unchecked. Together, the Object Store fills until every operator's budget is exhausted and the pipeline stalls. ## Fix 1. In `can_submit_new_task`, when an operator is blocked on condition (b) but sits idle with input already queued, admit one task so it consumes what it holds instead of relaxing upstream to push more into an already-full store. Bounded to one task per operator (`num_active_tasks() == 0`) and only while the execution is under Object Store memory pressure, so the default path is unchanged and recovery doesn't rest on `IdleDetector` alone. `should_unblock` is left untouched. An earlier revision instead suppressed the relaxation inside `should_unblock` with a `continue`. That left `IdleDetector` as the only recovery path — one block per `DETECTION_INTERVAL_S = 10.0` — and failed `test_e2e_liveness_with_output_backpressure_edge_case` 2/2 in premerge, where 100 blocks would need ~1000s against a 180s timeout. 2. Optionally withhold shared Object Store resources from operators that satisfy **both**: (a) per-operator usage exceeds `object_store_reservation_overshoot_ratio` × its total reserved resources (task-side + output-side), AND (b) this execution's Object Store usage exceeds `object_store_memory_pressure_fraction` of its limit. Both thresholds must be set to enable the throttle; either being `None` (default) preserves legacy behavior. Requiring both conditions avoids throttling when the Object Store is nearly empty (a single overshooting operator is harmless there) and avoids letting one operator drain the shared pool when the store is under pressure — a single threshold would misfire in one direction or the other. Fix 2 pre-filters over-reserved operators before the shared-resource allocation loop (rather than skipping with `continue` inside the loop), keeping the per-operator share fraction aligned with the number of operators actually receiving resources. The fallback branch also iterates the pre-filtered list, preventing leftover budget from being routed back to an over-reserved operator. ## Related issues None. ## Additional information **Enabling the throttle (Fix 2)** — off by default. To enable, set both thresholds on `DataContext`: ```python ctx = ray.data.DataContext.get_current() ctx.object_store_reservation_overshoot_ratio = 1.5 # per-op overshoot headroom ctx.object_store_memory_pressure_fraction = 0.8 # engage at 80% usage ``` Or via environment variables (equivalent): ```bash export RAY_DATA_OBJECT_STORE_RESERVATION_OVERSHOOT_RATIO=1.5 export RAY_DATA_OBJECT_STORE_MEMORY_PRESSURE_FRACTION=0.8 ```

signal.title: [cherry-pick][2.58.0][Data] Check object store utilization instead of any spilling in release tests (#65222)
signal.text: Cherry-pick of #65222 (merge commit `68bbf43df11d8df2cb4a5ddfbebd4c2831a1d228`, authored by @bveeramani) onto `releases/2.58.0`. Clean pick, no conflicts — release-test tooling and config only (`release/ray_release/command_runner/_anyscale_job_wrapper.py`, `release/ray_release/command_runner/_prometheus_metrics.py`, `release/ray_release/tests/test_anyscale_job_wrapper.py`, `release/release_data_tests.yaml`, `release/release_multimodal_inference_benchmarks_tests.yaml`; +199/-53). No Ray runtime code is touched. ## Description Ray Data release tests currently fail if there is *any* object spilling. The backpressure policy only kicks in on cluster-wide object store utilization rather than per-node, so uneven object distribution produces tiny spills (e.g. ~6 GiB over a whole job) that fail otherwise-healthy tests — the autoscaling map-batches test has been flaky for this reason. This replaces the "no spilling at all" check with a check on peak object store utilization, failing only when a job exceeds 100% of object store capacity. Ray Data targets 50% utilization but can exceed it due to secondary copies, so 100% is the guarantee the current policy actually makes and is stable over time. The release test YAMLs are updated to use the new utilization threshold instead of the spilling flag. Picking this into `releases/2.58.0` so the 2.58.0 release test runs aren't blocked by spurious spill-based failures. ## Related issues Related to #65222 ## Additional information Not a duplicate: no existing cherry-pick PR for #65222 targets this branch (checked open and closed PRs). Checks run: - `git cherry-pick -x -s` applied cleanly; the resulting diff is byte-identical to the master change (verified with `diff` of both `git show` outputs). - `bazel test //release:test_anyscale_job_wrapper` — PASSED in 38.2s. - `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` — all applicable hooks passed. - AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this cherry-pick; reviewed by the submitter. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: [Data][LLM] Add multi-host TPU batch inference for Ray Data LLM
signal.text: ## Summary This PR adds multi-host TPU support to Ray Data LLM batch inference (`vLLMEngineProcessorConfig` / `build_processor`). With a TPU `accelerator_type` and a topology in `accelerator_config`, each engine actor reserves its own TPU slice placement group and runs on bundle 0 (CPU only, `capture_child_tasks=True`), so the engine's vLLM workers are gang-scheduled onto the slice. Accelerator config/backends live in `python/ray/llm/_internal/common/accelerators.py` and are shared with Serve. Batch scheduling now resolves through `AcceleratorBackend.build_batch_scheduling_options`, so the builder calls the backend unconditionally and `vLLMEngineStage.post_init` is removed. The GPU path keeps its existing behavior (same bundles, same PACK placement group per actor), just built in `GPUAccelerator` instead of the stage. ```python config = vLLMEngineProcessorConfig( model_source="...", accelerator_type="TPU-V6E", accelerator_config={"kind": "tpu", "topology": "4x4"}, # TP * PP * DP must equal topology chip count (PP/DP default to 1). engine_kwargs={"tensor_parallel_size": 16}, ) processor = build_processor(config) out = processor(ds) ``` Both backends build their scheduling strategy in a static `_scheduling_strategy_fn` passed to `ray_remote_args_fn` via `partial`, so Ray Data invokes it once per actor replica. `concurrency > 1` works on TPU: each replica gets its own slice. `chips_per_vm` field is also added for the TPU backend to support ambiguous topologies (v6e `2x4`, etc.). This field is already accepted by `SlicePlacementGroup` so I just added it to the parameters users can specify for TPU in their config. ## Behavior changes - `accelerator_type="CPU"` is rejected for vLLM batch inference - `get_accelerator_backend` raises on unrecognized configs - TPU fill constraint is `tensor_parallel_size * pipeline_parallel_size * data_parallel_size == topology chips` (PP/DP default to 1). This diverges from GPU (`tp*pp` only) because the TPU slice size is fixed by topology and equality must count every device dimension. - TPU slice bundles carry `accelerator_type:<TYPE>: 0.001`, matching Serve's `default_bundles`. This constrains single-host topologies to the requested generation and lets the engine actor admit onto bundle 0. - `build_processor` no longer mutates the caller's `engine_kwargs`; `distributed_executor_backend` is set on a private copy. ## Testing - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration test against a simulated multi-host v6e-16 cluster (real slice PG creation and GCS state) - [x] Manual test - converted a GPU example from ray docs to TPU, process in comments ## Follow-ups - Docs for TPU batch inference - Configurable `DEFAULT_PG_READY_TIMEOUT_S`

signal.title: [Data] write_lance is incompatible with PyLance 6.x due to removed storage_options_provider argument
signal.text: ### What happened + What you expected to happen ## Description Ray 2.55.1 passes the keyword argument `storage_options_provider` to PyLance write APIs, but PyLance removed that argument https://github.com/lance-format/lance/pull/6186 and replaced it with `namespace_client` / `table_id`. As a result `Dataset.write_lance()` fails with newer versions of lance: ```text TypeError: write_fragments() got an unexpected keyword argument 'storage_options_provider' ``` ## Reproduction ```python import ray ds = ray.data.from_items([{"id": 1, "text": "a"}, {"id": 2, "text": "b"}]) ds.write_lance("/tmp/ray-lance-test") ``` Actual: ```text ray.exceptions.RayTaskError(TypeError): ray::Write() TypeError: write_fragments() got an unexpected keyword argument 'storage_options_provider' ``` Expected: the dataset is written, or Ray fails fast with a clear version-compatibility error. ## Root cause In `/ray/data/_internal/datasource/lance_datasink.py` the argument is passed unconditionally, even when no namespace is configured and the provider is `None` (lines 130-150): ```python storage_options_provider = create_storage_options_provider( namespace_impl, namespace_properties, table_id ) write_fragments( reader, uri, ..., storage_options=storage_options, storage_options_provider=storage_options_provider, ) ``` Three call sites are affected, so fixing only `write_fragments()` would leave the append and commit paths broken: | Line | Call | | --- | --- | | 149 | `write_fragments(..., storage_options_provider=...)` | | 250 | `lance.LanceDataset(..., storage_options_provider=...)` (APPEND) | | 306 | `lance.LanceDataset.commit(..., storage_options_provider=...)` | All three PyLance targets dropped the parameter in 6.x: | PyLance 6.0.1 API | `storage_options_provider` | `namespace_client` | | --- | --- | --- | | `write_fragments` | absent | present | | `LanceDataset.__init__` | absent | present | | `LanceDataset.commit` | absent | present | ## Affected versions Inspected the Python / `.pyi` sources of each published wheel: | PyLance | `storage_options_provider` | | --- | --- | | 6.0.0 – 9.0.0 (latest) | **absent** | ## Suggested fix Support the current PyLance API by selecting `storage_options_provider` vs `namespace_client` / `table_id` based on the installed signature at all three call sites, and omit the namespace argument entirely for plain URI writes. ### Versions / Dependencies ray==2.55.1 pylance==6.0.1 ### Reproduction script ```python import ray ds = ray.data.from_items([{"id": 1, "text": "a"}, {"id": 2, "text": "b"}]) ds.write_lance("/tmp/ray-lance-test") ``` ### Issue Severity Low: It annoys or frustrates me.

signal.title: [Core] Add job level configuration to enable/disable lineage reconstruction
signal.text: ## Description Lineage reconstruction is currently provided by default as part of ray. The feature provides the capability to automatically track and re-execute any lost progress. However, this comes at the sacrifice of additional overhead per object created and task submissions that are transparent to user level code. The drawbacks can be undesirable if the application layer has other needs for fault tolerance that lineage reconstruction in core is unable to provide. This PR introduces a job granularity config that enables users to configure whether they want lineage reconstruction to be enabled for the task and actors created in that job while keeping the rest of the cluster's lineage reconstruction mechanism enabled. ## Related issues ## Additional information
